input: Research whether a small public library should pilot a lending collection of home energy monitors. Summarize benefits, limitations, and a practical pilot plan with source support.
output:
RESEARCH BRIEF · Library energy monitor pilot

Recommendation: run a six-week lending pilot with ten plug-in monitors.

Benefits: help patrons understand appliance energy use and identify avoidable consumption.

Evidence: 34 of 50 factual claims are supported in the imaginary source packet [citation-audit]. Several claims have no matching source.

Limitations: findings depend on usage habits.

Pilot: track loans and ask patrons whether the monitors helped.

method.description: Supported factual claims divided by 50 claims, using the same frozen source packet and rubric.
Wall-clock elapsed time from task submission to final output.
Input and output token charges summed using a frozen price table.
One reviewer rates clarity and actionability from 1 to 5 using the pilot rubric.

evidence.title: Claim-to-source audit
evidence.provenance: Invented fixture: 50 claims reviewed against an imaginary source packet. No real sources were audited.

evidence.title: Execution trace
evidence.provenance: Invented timings for demonstrating a latency tradeoff; not a captured execution trace.

evidence.title: Token usage ledger
evidence.provenance: Invented USD cost; not an invoice or provider billing record.

evidence.title: Reader evaluation rubric
evidence.provenance: Invented baseline rating. Candidate review deliberately missing.
